summary: Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a tibetologist who founded the STTAR series and Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region. He served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983-1991) and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center starting in 2000.
Liang Cai works in sinology and history and archaeology. Cai studied under Daniel Boucher and was attested as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas in 2014.
Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, attested in 2011.

Lilian Silburn (1908-1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo (1948). She held positions at the National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) from circa 1945 to 1978 and taught André Padoux.

Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under M. Sri Rammandala and traditional teacher Julius Berugoda, and taught Douglas Osto and Pahalawattage Don Premasiri. She held posts at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1970 and 2008.
Lin He (1902-1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from circa 1919 to 1926. He held a post there from circa 1931 to 1937 and taught Jiyu Ren.
Lin Heng is an Indologist who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, attested in 2015.

Linda Hogan is a religious studies scholar who earned a BA at Maynooth and a PhD from Trinity College Dublin (-1991). She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, where she served as Vice-Provost and Chief Academic Officer (2011-2016).
Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe, attested in 2001.
Linda Learman works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory, both attested in 2005.

Linda Penkower specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned a PhD from Columbia University in 1993, held a research fellowship at Taisho University attested in 1983, and taught Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007) as well as Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is a scholar of sinology who served as a professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo, attested in 2014.

Linnart Mäll (1938-2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957-1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1965-1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu from circa 1969 to 2010.

Lionel David Barnett (1871-1960) was an Indologist educated at Liverpool and Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1899-1936, 1948) as Keeper, taught at SOAS (1917-1948) and UCL (1906-1917), and taught Arthur Llewellyn Basham.

Lionel Obadia is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He held positions at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910-2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Liu held posts at West China Union University, the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, and the Ethnic Publishing House.

Lisa Grumbach is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Stanford University, attested in 1996, and has served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995 and earned an MA and PhD (-2006) at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Janice Leoshko.
